newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo Nobel says too early for 97 forecast.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel says too early for 97 forecast.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel said Wednesday it expected the economy to pick up in 1997, but that it was too early to give a forecast of 1997 earnings.
"Akzo Nobel will not issue a profit forecast (for 1997) until mid-way through next year," a spokeswoman said.
Dutch financial daily Het Financieele Dagblad said on Wednesday Akzo Nobel Chairman Cees van Lede had told a meeting of analysts on Tuesday that 1997 would be a strong year, albeit not a record one.
But Akzo said the comment should not be taken to refer to the company's profit outlook as suggested by the article.

"During the analysts' meeting...Cees van Lede...made a statement referring to general economic developments and (was) certainly not referring specifically to Akzo Nobel," the company said in statement.
The spokeswoman said that for 1996 the company was maintaining its November forecast that full-year net profit before extraordinaries would be about level with that of 1995.
The statement quoted Van Lede as saying that in the year 2000, chemicals and coatings would account for roughly the same proportion of total sales as at present.

"The percentage of sales generated by pharmaceuticals could rise by a magnitude of 20-25 percent, (while) the percentage of sales generated by fibres will likely fall by some 10 percent," it quoted Van Lede as saying.

In the first nine months of 1996, chemicals accounted for some 34 percent of sales and coatings for 33 percent, while fibres accounted for around 15 percent and high-margin pharmaceuticals for 17 percent of sales.

The media reports of Van Lede's comments boosted Akzo's shares on an otherwise sharply lower Amsterdam bourse. By 1100 GMT Akzo was up 2.40 guilders to 234.40. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
